questions.question_text: Under RSA 356-B, how many units trigger the Public Offering Statement registration requirement when marketed to the public?
questions.explanation: A condominium is exempt from registration and Public Offering Statement requirements if not more than 10 units are included in the project, unless time-sharing interests are involved (RSA 356-B:49). The threshold for triggering full registration is therefore more than 10 units. A 'small condominium' of 25 or fewer units may still qualify for abbreviated registration under RSA 356-B:51.

questions.question_text: A developer plans a 3-unit condominium project. What registration obligation applies under RSA 356-B?
questions.correct_answer: The project is exempt from registration and POS requirements
distractors: A full POS must be filed with the AG
The developer must obtain a DES permit
questions.explanation: Condominium offerings of not more than 10 units are exempt from the chapter's registration and Public Offering Statement requirements, unless time-sharing interests are involved or the structure is being used to evade the law (RSA 356-B:49). A 3-unit project falls well within that exemption, although condominium instruments still must be recorded with the Registry of Deeds.

questions.question_text: Which state office reviews condominium Public Offering Statements in New Hampshire?
questions.explanation: The Attorney General's Consumer Protection and Antitrust Bureau administers RSA 356-B and reviews Public Offering Statements for condominium projects that exceed the 10-unit RSA 356-B:49 exemption.

questions.question_text: Where must condominium instruments be recorded in New Hampshire?
questions.explanation: Condominium instruments (declaration, bylaws, site plans, and floor plans) must be recorded with the county Registry of Deeds under RSA 356-B.

questions.question_text: A buyer purchases a condo unit in NH. What ownership interest does the buyer receive in the common areas?
questions.correct_answer: An undivided interest in common areas
distractors: A leasehold interest in common areas
A tenancy at will in common areas
questions.explanation: Under the NH Condominium Act (RSA 356-B), condo owners hold fee simple title to their individual unit plus an undivided interest in the common areas of the condominium.

questions.question_text: Under RSA 477:44, when does manufactured housing become real estate in NH?
questions.correct_answer: When placed on site and connected to utilities
distractors: When the owner obtains a building permit
When the title is transferred at the DMV
When the home is older than 10 years
questions.explanation: Manufactured housing is deemed real estate when it is placed on a site AND tied into required utilities (RSA 477:44). It is then conveyed, mortgaged, and encumbered with the same formalities as real estate. Note that New Hampshire uses statutory-form deeds (not DMV certificates of title) for manufactured housing transfers generally — RSA 477:44, III requires a deed even for a transfer occurring before utility connection.

questions.question_text: A manufactured housing park owner receives an acceptable offer to buy the park. Under RSA 205-A:21, how many days' notice must tenants receive before the owner may finally accept the offer?
questions.explanation: Under RSA 205-A:21, a park owner may not make a final unconditional acceptance of an offer to sell the park without first giving each tenant 60 days' notice of the intent to sell and of the price, terms, and conditions of the acceptable offer. During that period the owner must consider any offer from the tenants or a tenants' association and negotiate in good faith — but the statute does not give tenants a right of first refusal to match the offer.

questions.question_text: A park owner raises rent without proper notice. How many days advance notice is required under RSA 205-A?
questions.explanation: Park owners must give 60 days advance notice for rent increases (RSA 205-A). The notice must clearly state the new amount and the effective date.

questions.question_text: A manufactured housing park is being sold. What right do current tenants have under NH law?
questions.correct_answer: 60 days' notice plus good-faith negotiation of a tenant offer
distractors: The right to block the sale entirely
The right to a reduced purchase price
No rights in the park sale process
questions.explanation: Under RSA 205-A:21, before making a final unconditional acceptance of an offer, the park owner must give each tenant 60 days' notice including the price, terms, and conditions of the acceptable offer, must consider any purchase offer from the tenants or a tenants' association, and must negotiate with them in good faith; tenants get reasonable extra time beyond the 60 days to arrange financing. This is a notice-and-negotiation right, not a right of first refusal — tenants cannot block the sale, and a sale made without notice remains valid, with the owner liable instead for a civil penalty under RSA 205-A:22.

questions.question_text: How does RSA 205-A define a manufactured housing park?
questions.correct_answer: Two or more manufactured houses on a site
distractors: Five or more manufactured houses on a site
Ten or more manufactured houses on a site
Any land zoned for manufactured housing
questions.explanation: A manufactured housing park is a property with two or more manufactured houses (RSA 205-A). This low threshold means most multi-unit manufactured housing sites are subject to the park regulations.
